CT561 Paper-Based Topic Guide

Stock Management and Workforce Models

Anchor-and-adjustment structures, staff recruitment, target changes and ageing chains recur across the paper archive and remain explicit in 2024/25 and 2025/26.

Question families to prepare

  • Explain the structure [5-7]: distinguish adjustment to a goal from stock management; define anchor, adjustment and the delay used for expected losses.
  • Design staff recruitment [10-12]: full equations, desired staff from a ratio, hires, quits/attrition and feedbacks.
  • Sketch a target shock [5-8]: predict actual staff, ratio, expected losses or an ageing chain after a changed target.

References: 2023/24 Q2(b,c), 2024/25 Q2(a-c), 2025/26 Q4(b-d), plus 2017/18 Q4(c-e), 2018/19 Q4 and 2021/22 Q1(c).

Anchor and adjustment

A plain adjustment-to-a-goal structure only closes the target gap:

Adjustment = (Desired Stock - Actual Stock)/Adjustment Time

Stock management adds an anchor to replace expected normal losses:

Expected Losses = SMOOTH(Actual Losses, Expectation Adjustment Time)
Required Inflow = Expected Losses + Adjustment

At equilibrium, Actual Stock = Desired Stock, so Adjustment = 0 and Required Inflow = Expected Losses. The anchor is a first-order smoothing/delay structure; the adjustment is a balancing goal-seeking structure.

2024/25 University recruitment model [12]

Students = INTEG(Recruitments - Graduations, 10000)
Desired Staff = Students / Desired Student Staff Ratio
Staff = INTEG(Hires - Quits, 500)
Quits = Quit Fraction x Staff
Expected Quits = SMOOTH(Quits, Expectation Adjustment Time)
Hires = Expected Quits + (Desired Staff - Staff)/Staff Adjustment Time

Initially Desired Staff = 10,000/20 = 500, matching actual Staff. When the desired student-to-staff ratio falls from 20 to 10 at time 10, desired staff immediately becomes 1,000. The discrepancy is +500, hires rise above quits, and Staff rises smoothly towards 1,000.

Sketch answer: Staff is flat at 500 until time 10, then rises at a decreasing rate and approaches 1,000. The staff adjustment time is the auxiliary with the strongest direct influence on settling speed. A shorter time means a faster and potentially unrealistic recruitment response.

Ageing-chain workforce model [10]

2025/26 Q4(c) uses Trainee, Experienced and Senior staff. Draw three stocks with progression pipes and attrition outflows:

Trainees = INTEG(Hires - Progression TE - Attrition T, 100)
Experienced = INTEG(Progression TE - Progression ES - Attrition E, 100)
Seniors = INTEG(Progression ES - Attrition S, 100)
Progression TE = Trainees/12; Progression ES = Experienced/36
Attrition T = 0.05 x Trainees; Attrition E = 0.03 x Experienced; Attrition S = 0.01 x Seniors
Total Staff = Trainees + Experienced + Seniors

Set Hires from the stock-management rule using Total Staff. A target reduction from 300 to 100 makes the adjustment negative. If there is no explicit dismissal flow, Hires should fall to zero or be bounded at zero, and attrition/progression gradually reduce the total.

Target-change behaviour

  • If desired staff rises, discrepancy becomes positive, hires rise and staff approaches the higher target.
  • If desired staff falls, discrepancy becomes negative, hiring should fall. The speed of reduction is limited by exits unless a dismissal flow is added.
  • Expected losses lag actual losses because they are smoothed; explain that lag on sketches.
  • A pipeline or ageing chain introduces more delay and can create overshoot if decisions ignore people already progressing.

Mark checklist

  • Desired staff uses Students / desired student-to-staff ratio, not the reverse.
  • Anchor replaces expected losses; adjustment closes the target gap.
  • Hires and quits are flows; Staff and pipeline stages are stocks.
  • Show the balancing feedback and label adjustment/expectation times.
  • On a sketch, label the shock time, direction, new equilibrium and any lag.
